Let’s fix science.

Every discovery starts with something we take on trust. Nobody has time to check everything. AI is changing what we can afford to verify.

We invite volunteers everywhere to donate computing time. Together, let’s check the claims that thousands of studies build on.

Paste it into your AI. It will ask how much you want to contribute and how often.

Read the prompt 
Help me contribute to Let’s Fix Science. Your first reply should be one question that covers scope and timing:

“How much would you like to contribute, and is this one-time or recurring? You can choose a review depth, a paper count, or a time or computing budget. For example, five focused reviews once, or two hours of in-depth checks every week.”

Wait for my answer before reserving a paper, submitting anything or creating a schedule. Respect the amount I choose. Use the depth I choose or a depth suited to my stated budget. The API accepts quick, standard or deep.

If I request recurring work, confirm any missing frequency, local time and time zone. Schedule only with my authorization, using my AI client’s real scheduler. Check for an existing matching task before creating one. Verify its task ID and next local run. Tell me if this client cannot schedule it. A scheduled run uses the agreed budget and instructions below, starting when agreed.

For each authorized run:
1. Reserve one paper at a time. POST JSON to https://lets-fix-science.vercel.app/api/agent with action="claim", effort, model and request_id. Omit contributor. Use the actual model and version if known, otherwise model="undisclosed". Generate a secret UUIDv4 locally per reservation. Reuse it on retries.
2. For quick, recalculate a number or compare a passage with its source. For standard, test one complete claim against the evidence. For deep, check alternative assumptions and sensitivity where feasible. Cite the published page, table, figure or equation. Compare expected and observed results. Respect the agreed depth, number of papers and time or computing limit.
3. Submit privately to the same endpoint with action="submit", assignment_id, token, outcome, claim, method, result, limits and source_url. Use the returned assignment_id and token, and a primary HTTPS source. Choose "matches", "discrepancy" or "inconclusive". Return each actual receipt privately to me. Continue sequentially only within my agreed scope.
4. Use public material. Exclude contact details and private data. Do not contact authors or publish findings. Keep credentials private. If connectivity or submission fails, tell me what remains unconfirmed.
Default prompt as plain text

What counts as a check?

A check can repeat a calculation or compare a claim with the published text.

Each paper counts once. Earlier checks cover 58 papers in this ranking. Independent verification requires a separate, documented check against the source.

52 papers have only private test records. The total includes this private work. Its details stay confidential. Each square shows only public information.

How the totals work

Each public paper contributes its verified citation count once, under its main observed issue. A citing work can cite several audited papers. These totals measure citation links; establishing which subsequent results depend on the questioned claim requires reading those works.

We exclude findings the audit has rectified from these sums. Missing counts stay separate from verified zeroes.

Frequently asked questions

A guide to reading the findings and contributing evidence.

How do you check an observation?

We choose a specific claim from a peer-reviewed paper. We compare it with the available data, calculations or code, look for alternative explanations and contact the authors. Each record sets out the evidence and its limits.

How do you choose papers?

We look for claims that can be checked using the study materials. We now prioritize historically highly cited papers. This targeted selection cannot establish how common errors are across science.

Can I see an example?

A study tested whether its model could classify new data. We ran its code with 200 simulated rows. It trained on all 200, including the 20 held out for each test. The test therefore used data the model had already seen. The effect on real-world performance needs a fresh evaluation. Read the finding.

When does a finding become public?

First we verify that we sent the inquiry to the authors. We wait ten full days after sending, even if nobody replies. The record appears at the next update. Waiting papers appear only as an aggregate count.

What happens when authors reply?

We check their explanation against the evidence and update the status. We record a published correction once verified. If nobody replies, the question remains open. Individual emails stay private.

Does a finding invalidate the entire study?

It depends on which results used the calculation or method in question. A table can require correction while other conclusions still hold. Read “What could change” for the scope of each finding.

How can I request a correction?

Include the record ID and a public source. We review the evidence and amend the finding when warranted. Please share only public information. Open a public inquiry on GitHub.

Original paper ↗
Evidence and limits

Where to look

Results: Humans give more viruses to animals; exclusion prayer SARS-CoV-2/ MERS / Influenza. Code anthroponotic_frequency.distinct_nodes.R:161–208.Supplementaryand Table3.

Evidence

  • SupplementaryTable3 reproduces 2904 total leaps, 599 humans: 383 anthroponotic and 216 zoonotic.
  • To exclude the four declared cliques leave 327 events: 175 anthroponotic and 152 zoonotic, 53,5168% frente46,4832%.
  • The code reSamples events and applying .paired test at1000 pairs bootstrap. The difference bootstrap has ley2 * Binomial (327,175 / 327) − 327.
  • That distribution has mediates23, deviation 18.0383553 and exact interval 95% [− 13.59]. Divide by sqrt (1000) explain t expected 40,32096, close to published t40.
  • La expresión t.test original se ejecutó por parseR con remuestreo baseR explícito: t37.57,df999,p2.74e−193, intervalo[−15,59]. No reproduce la realización MonteCarlo editorial.
  • Binomial diagnosis by event: p.223699 and does not constitute a definitive phylogenetic p. The published global permutation .035 remains as separate evidence.

Limits

  • Exact175/152 counts and53.5% reproduce SupplementaryTable3 and the declared exclusions.
  • The original1000 Monte Carlo draws are unavailable; fresh draws are not the editorial realization.
  • The binomial test is an illustrative event-level sensitivity, without viral-clique dependence adjustment.
  • The exact bootstrap interval follows the pooled-event code; Methods describes within-clique resampling.
  • No phylogenies, host-state inference, full global permutation test, or biological transmission rates are reconstructed.
  • The separate full-data permutation p=.035 and observed64%/36% result are not refuted.
  • The nonsignificant sensitivity does not prove equal frequencies or reverse the observed direction.
  • No misstatement was attributed to the global operator and biological differences of adaptation.
  • The sinSARS / FLU permutation script conserving MERS does not exactly represent the four exclusions.
  • The related News & Views only offered preview by subscription and was not fully revised.

  • En 200 individuos sintéticos, cambiar desenlaces externos modifica las probabilidades reajustadas.
  • El cambio absoluto medio es 0.08037; las predicciones entrenadas permanecen idénticas.
  • La contrarrevisión ML confirma que se sustituyen probabilidades, más allá de estimar pendientes.
  • No ejecutamos rms ni sus 1.000 remuestreos; tampoco reconstruimos curvas clínicas.

Limits

  • No reconstruimos probabilidades ni curvas de los pacientes publicados.
  • No cuantificamos descalibración real ni sus consecuencias clínicas.
  • El C-index y AUC utilizan una ruta separada. Sus cifras permanecen sin refutación.
  • La demostración numérica utiliza datos sintéticos y Cox equivalente, con adaptador declarado.
  • Una implementación distinta utilizada para Figure 5 podría resolver la objeción.
  • El ajuste con outcomes test en IBS.R es corroboración secundaria, sin fidelidad numérica publicada.

  • Control with 100000 rows uses 64 copies to limit memory.
  • The main test uses 1000 replicas with original size and isolates the inconsequential error.

  • The absence of a localised public priority does not show complete novelties.

Where to look

Theorem 3.2 and Appendix Theorem D.3.

Evidence

  • Set d=2, p=1, h=id and weights w_n=6/(pi^2*n^2).
  • Points s_n=(4*n^2/(n^4+4),0,(n^4-4)/(n^4+4)) lie in S2 minus the north pole.
  • Their stereographic images are (n^2,0).
  • The probability measure sum w_n delta_s_n has finite spherical first moment.

  • Finite empirical data and bounded/capped implementations are not refuted.

What the study claimed

La prueba entre particiones respalda mejoras al predecir mutismo cerebeloso posoperatorio.

Observation

Wilcoxon trata los resultados de 100 folds repetidos como diferencias independientes. Los mismos 204 sujetos aparecen diez veces en evaluación. Bajo igualdad poblacional, el procedimiento rechaza mucho más que el 5% nominal.

What could change

La ventaja estadística puede desaparecer al contar una sola vez a cada niño.

Where to look

  • Methods, Statistical Analysis: prueba Wilcoxon pareada sobre validación cruzada de 10 repeticiones y 10 folds.
  • Abstract, Results y Figure 1: superioridad significativa de ANN frente a regresión logística.
  • notebooks/analysis.ipynb: results acumula una métrica por fold; print_metric_significance ejecuta scipy.stats.wilcoxon.
  • src/crossvalidate.cc: todos los sujetos participan una vez por repetición en evaluación.
  • Notebook, salida archivada Number of runs:100; comparación ANN versus LR.

Evidence

  • El generador original evalúa cada sujeto diez veces entre cien folds.
  • Reejecutamos la comparación Wilcoxon original con las mismas particiones.
  • Simulamos 2.000 cohortes independientes, con igual accuracy poblacional esperada para ambos clasificadores.
  • El procedimiento rechaza 1.065 cohortes: 53,25%, frente al 5% nominal.
  • El intervalo exacto del porcentaje de rechazo es [51,03%; 55,46%].
  • No entrenamos la red ni calculamos valores p clínicos corregidos.

Limits

  • Los datos clínicos y las predicciones individuales originales no son públicos.
  • No reentrenamos la ANN ni calculamos valores p clínicos corregidos.
  • La simulación nula emplea clasificadores fijos con igual desempeño esperado por estrato.
  • Las particiones se mantienen independientes de las predicciones simuladas.
  • El generador C++ original permanece intacto. Su almacenamiento y barajado usan un shim documentado.
  • El shim FANN no implementa entrenamiento neuronal.
  • La aleatorización por sujeto y Wilcoxon tienen nulos distintos. No equiparamos sus estimandos.
  • La simulación de error tipo I evalúa directamente el nulo poblacional pertinente.
  • No refutamos las métricas puntuales ni negamos una posible ventaja clínica verdadera.
  • La salida archivada p=.055 es evidencia adicional, sujeta a límites de versión.

Original wording in the audit record

What the study claimed

La covarianza posterior escalada recupera la proyección tangente sobre el soporte.

Observation

Soporte completo y densidad C3 no implican densidad estrictamente positiva. En un cero cuadrático, la covarianza posterior escalada recupera tres veces la proyección tangente.

What could change

Una densidad que se anula puede cambiar la escala del estimador geométrico.

Where to look

Theorem 1, Eq. 5, página 6. Corollary 2, página 7. Appendix E.4, página 33, inferencia incorrecta sobre cotas positivas.

Evidence

La posterior angular es proporcional a (1−cosθ)exp(cosθ/σ²). Por simetría, su media tangente vale cero. Con κ=1/σ², Var(sinθ)/σ²=(I1(κ)−I2(κ))/(I0(κ)−I1(κ)). Ese cociente converge a 3. La proyección tangente verdadera tiene componente 1 en esa dirección. Por tanto, el error de operador tiene límite inferior 2. Eq. 5 exige convergencia a cero, pues Kσ|logσ|³→0 para cualquier K fijo.

Limits

La contraprueba usa un cero aislado de la densidad, de probabilidad µ nula. No demuestra fallo en todos los puntos ni resultados experimentales incorrectos. Una hipótesis reforzada de positividad estricta excluye este ejemplo. No refutamos algoritmos bajo esa hipótesis adicional.

The code sampling levels with p_l proportional to s_l= (2nu / ell ² + l (l +1))1). It uses characteristics proportional to sqrt (2l +1)P_l(or · x). The uniform integral of P_l(u·x)P_l(g) es P_l(x·y)/(2l+1). Thus its limitation covariance is proportional to suma_l s_l P_l(x · and). The declared Mast requires suma_l (2l+1)s_l P_l(x) and) with nu = 1, lt = 1 and two levels, s0 = 1/4 y s1 = 1/16. The correlation between antipods of the code converts to 0.6. The target covariance has a correlation 1/7with the 24 level, their respective co-relations are 0.590615 y 0.192904. No global constant fixes this spectral reason.

Página 15, Equation 31. Código src/DRF/layers.py, clase RandomPhaseFeatureMap, líneas 183–264.

Evidence

El código muestrea niveles con p_l proporcional a s_l=(2nu/ell²+l(l+1))^(-nu-1). Usa características proporcionales a sqrt(2l+1)P_l(u·x). La integral uniforme de P_l(u·x)P_l(u·y) es P_l(x·y)/(2l+1). Por tanto, su covarianza límite es proporcional a suma_l s_l P_l(x·y). La Matérn declarada requiere suma_l (2l+1)s_l P_l(x·y). Con nu = 1, ell = 1 y dos niveles, s0 = 1/4 y s1 = 1/16. La correlación entre antípodas del código converge a 0.6. La covarianza objetivo tiene correlación 1/7. Con los 24 niveles predeterminados, las correlaciones respectivas son 0.590615 y 0.192904. Ninguna constante global corrige esta razón espectral.

Limits

No reejecutamos entrenamiento ni cuantificamos cambios de precisión geofísica. Comparamos el prior y su aproximación publicada. Los errores adicionales de constantes y argumentos del apéndice no sostienen el hallazgo principal.
